purpose: The ~34 canonical concepts of the current BANZA architecture (M2.19A-F.2), each grounded in the real ADR/schema/engine that defines it, with the public route that should OWN the definition, the reference chapters that may repeat it, the forbidden legacy terms that must never re-enter its surface, its states and its relations. Every normative_source was verified against decisions/adr/*.md headers and contracts/**/*.json.

architecture_baseline.L1: BANZA Protocol — open, neutral, verifiable (ADR-059 D-059-01)
architecture_baseline.L2: Conformance & Interoperability Certification — per-implementation, evidence-based, Rust-decided (ADR-059 D-059-02, ADR-064)
architecture_baseline.L3: Banzami Operational Scheme — designated operator, regulatory-authorization-in-progress, real money OFF (ADR-059 D-059-03, ADR-060, ADR-062)
architecture_baseline.BanzAI: single human-operator interface at /banzai, transversal across the three layers, NOT a fourth layer/authority (ADR-059 D-059-04, ADR-054, ADR-067)
architecture_baseline.authority_rule: Rust decides; Qwen explains once and never decides (ADR-059 D-059-05, ADR-037)

concepts.name: BANZA
concepts.short_def: The open, neutral, verifiable financial protocol (Layer 1). Rules, not a product.
concepts.full_def: BANZA is the open financial protocol of Angola: public rules, contracts, messages, schemas, APIs, invariants, reason codes, technical identity, manifests, signatures, discovery, profiles, Signed Protocol Metadata, trust, revocation, the technical registry, federation and public verification. It is not a bank, PSP, wallet, e-money institution or operator; it holds/moves no funds, runs no accounts, settles nothing, issues no licences and replaces no regulator or scheme.
concepts.normative_source: ADR-001 (open financial protocol), ADR-059 D-059-01 (Layer 1 definition), ADR-002 (ecosystem naming)
relations: BANZA is Layer 1; certification (L2) and scheme (L3) sit above it

concepts.name: protocolo financeiro aberto
concepts.short_def: The category BANZA belongs to: an open, operator-neutral rules layer for payment interoperability.
concepts.full_def: An open financial protocol is a public, operator-neutral specification (contracts + invariants + conformance) that independent operators implement to interoperate and produce verifiable evidence, with no bilateral integration and no central human approval. Analogous to HTTP/SMTP but for payments.
concepts.normative_source: ADR-001 (implementation independence), CLAUDE.md operator-neutrality invariant, ADR-059 D-059-01
relations: enables federation without prior bilateral agreements per operator pair

concepts.name: entidade operadora / operador
concepts.short_def: An independent legal entity that implements the protocol and processes payments under its own authorisations.
concepts.full_def: An operator is any independent legal entity that implements BANZA to process payments in its own systems, under its own regulatory authorisations. At the protocol plane it is subject only to conformance verification (the same deterministic public tests for all); outside the protocol it carries all legal, regulatory, banking, KYC/KYB and AML/CFT obligations, which are entirely its own. BANZA is not an operator.
concepts.normative_source: ADR-003 (operator separation), ADR-010 (account/participant identity), ADR-039 (self-publication), ch.8 of the reference
relations: publishes an Operator Manifest + Signed Protocol Metadata + conformance evidence
an operator's implementation is the subject of certification (L2)
may be a scheme participant (L3) — a separate determination

concepts.name: implementação
concepts.short_def: The subject of certification: a specific build/artifact set, identified by content hash — never an entity or brand.
concepts.full_def: A CertifiedImplementation is identified by a stable implementation_id plus implementation_hash (the content hash of the exact artifact set tested). The certificate binds to that hash, so a different build is a different subject needing its own certification. The declaring party (declared_by) is attribution/contact only, never the subject.
concepts.normative_source: ADR-064 D-064-01, contracts/production/certified-implementation.production.schema.json
concepts.canonical_page: /certificacao (MISSING — real page to be built; today redirects to /referencia/certificacao)

concepts.name: implementação de referência
concepts.short_def: Operador Zero: the single canonical, read-only reference implementation of the protocol.
concepts.full_def: A reference implementation exposes how an implementation presents itself (identity, manifest, capabilities, endpoints, metadata, keys, reports, evidence, certification status) and nothing else. Operador Zero is the single canonical reference implementation; it is read-only and runs no simulation, mutable ledger, conformance/trust/federation execution, evidence-bundle construction or certification action. It responds to protocol messages and external tests; it never tests or certifies itself.
concepts.normative_source: ADR-067 D-067-01 (read-only reference), ADR-052 (reference implementation), ADR-053 (Operator-Zero-only policy)
relations: validated only in BanzAI validation mode with target=operator-zero
never a real operator, never in /operators, never a scheme participant

concepts.name: participante de scheme
concepts.short_def: An entity/implementation admitted as a participant of a specific operational scheme (Layer 3).
concepts.full_def: A scheme participant is an entity/implementation that a specific scheme (the Banzami Operational Scheme, or any independent scheme) has admitted under that scheme's own due diligence, eligibility and contracts. Membership of the L3 participant directory is separate from the L2 Technical Registry; it may require valid certification but is never implied by it.
concepts.normative_source: ADR-060 D-060-06, ADR-061 D-061-02 (Scheme Admission)
concepts.canonical_page: /arquitectura (three-layer) — L3 participant directory is out of this repo's public surface

concepts.name: perfil / Certification Profile
concepts.short_def: The public, versioned yardstick an implementation is certified against.
concepts.full_def: An InteroperabilityCertificationProfile names, for a given conformance level and capability set, the exact conformance suites, interoperability vectors, required schemas/contracts/invariants/endpoints, identity/signature/trust requirements and validity window an implementation must satisfy — each pinned by content hash. Immutable once published (a change is a new profile_version). Derived only from L1 protocol contracts; introduces no operator-specific criteria.
concepts.normative_source: ADR-064 D-064-02, contracts/production/certification-profile.production.schema.json
relations: consumes conformance suites and interoperability vectors

concepts.name: capability
concepts.short_def: A protocol surface an implementation declares it implements — descriptive, not a grant.
concepts.full_def: A capability is a named protocol surface (e.g. 'payment-intents', 'qr', 'federation') that a candidate declares in its Operator Manifest and that a certification profile requires. It describes intended/demonstrated behaviour; it is not a permission or a grant. A CertificationRecord's scope_capabilities are never broader than the evidence.
concepts.normative_source: contracts/production/operator-manifest.production.schema.json (capabilities), ADR-064 (scope_capabilities)

concepts.name: Operator Manifest
concepts.short_def: The self-published artifact by which a candidate operator identifies itself to the protocol.
concepts.full_def: The Operator Manifest declares operator_id, environment, simulated flag, production_allowed, capabilities, key_manifest_url, protocol_version, base_url, supported_levels and the operator's own regulatory declaration. production_allowed asserts only that the operator's OWN regulator authorised it (validated by that authority, never by BANZA). A manifest never activates a real operator.
concepts.normative_source: ADR-039 (self-publication), contracts/production/operator-manifest.production.schema.json
relations: points to the key manifest and conformance evidence
verified during discovery + Open Trust Evaluation
bound by an Evidence Bundle manifest_hash

concepts.name: discovery
concepts.short_def: Step 1 of validation: locating and reading an implementation's self-published protocol surface.
concepts.full_def: Discovery is the act of finding and reading an implementation's public, self-published protocol surface (well-known endpoints, manifest, metadata) with no BANZA account and no central lookup. It is the first of the nine validation steps and a precondition for trust evaluation.
concepts.normative_source: ADR-039 (operator self-publication), ADR-038 (open trust model / well-known), ADR-067 D-067-02 (step 1 of the 9-step journey)

concepts.name: key manifest
concepts.short_def: The published set of PUBLIC signing keys and their domains — never private keys.
concepts.full_def: A key manifest publishes only public keys and their domains (root, issuing, revocation), validity windows and a content hash for tamper-evidence. Private keys never appear and are never transmitted. At M2_PROTOCOL_IMPLEMENTATION no real production keys exist: keys are prepared-but-gated placeholders until the offline root-key ceremony. Publishing a key manifest activates no operator and moves no funds.
concepts.normative_source: ADR-028 (keys never on serving infrastructure), ADR-038 (trust model), contracts/production/key-manifest.production.schema.json

concepts.name: Signed Protocol Metadata
concepts.short_def: Protocol metadata signed by the Trust Root (or delegated keys) — an assertion about ARTIFACTS, never participants.
concepts.full_def: Signed Protocol Metadata is metadata signed by the Trust Root or by Delegated Signing Keys under it. The Trust Root signs exactly four object classes: protocol metadata, protocol releases, delegated signing keys and the Revocation List. A signature is an assertion about protocol artifacts, never about a participant — it authorises no payments, creates no operators, issues no licences and certifies no operator. Verified under a 2-of-3 threshold with fail-closed semantics.
concepts.normative_source: ADR-038 D-038 / INV-OTE-001, contracts/production/signed-protocol-metadata.production.schema.json
relations: input to the Open Trust Evaluation (trust)
verified against delegated keys endorsed by root metadata

concepts.name: conformance
concepts.short_def: Deterministic, reproducible verification that an implementation respects the protocol contracts and invariants.
concepts.full_def: Conformance is the deterministic, public, reproducible verification (suites + vectors) that an implementation obeys the protocol's contracts, schemas and financial invariants for a given scope. Its output is a hash-bound conformance report/evidence a third party re-runs to reproduce the hashes. A PASS is verifiable evidence, not certification, licence or authorisation.
concepts.normative_source: ADR-021 (conformance level/capability alignment), ADR-064 (certification consumes conformance), engines/banza-conformance, contracts/production/conformance-report.production.schema.json
relations: scope expressed in conformance levels L0-L4 (technical scope only, not a public certification tier)

concepts.name: interoperability
concepts.short_def: Verified ability of independent implementations to exchange payments under the same rules without bilateral integration.
concepts.full_def: Interoperability is the verified capacity of independent conformant implementations to route/settle payments between each other under the same invariants, established by evidence + Open Trust Evaluation rather than per-pair contracts. In the L2 model it is measured by interoperability vectors and reported in an InteroperabilityReport, feeding the certification verdict.
concepts.normative_source: ADR-064 (Conformance & Interoperability Certification), ADR-040 (federation trust evaluation), contracts/openapi/interoperability-certification.yaml, contracts/production/interoperability-report.production.schema.json

concepts.name: certification
concepts.short_def: Layer 2: a per-implementation, evidence-based, Rust-decided determination against a public versioned profile.
concepts.full_def: BANZA Conformance & Interoperability Certification (Layer 2) is a per-implementation, evidence-based, Rust-decided, reproducible, hash-bound, scoped and time-limited determination that an implementation demonstrated conformance and interoperability against a public, versioned profile, subject to suspension/revocation. It certifies an implementation, never an entity, and confers no status beyond 'this implementation passed this profile at this version with this evidence'. It is NOT a licence, NOT scheme admission and NOT regulatory authorisation.
relations: L2 = the SECOND institutional layer (not a level)

concepts.name: CertifiedImplementation
concepts.short_def: The subject object of a certificate — an implementation bound to its artifact content hash.
concepts.full_def: See 'implementação'. CertifiedImplementation is the canonical object naming the subject of certification: implementation_id + implementation_hash, with declared_by as attribution only. A different build is a different subject.
concepts.normative_source: ADR-064 D-064-01, contracts/production/certified-implementation.production.schema.json

concepts.name: Certification Record
concepts.short_def: The verdict object: binds an implementation to a profile with evidence, scope, validity window, state and record hash.
concepts.full_def: A CertificationRecord binds a CertifiedImplementation (by implementation_hash) to an InteroperabilityCertificationProfile (by profile_id+profile_version), carrying the reproducible evidence hashes (conformance report + evidence bundle), the Rust-decided verdict, a status + reason_code, the scope (levels/capabilities, never broader than evidence), a validity window (issued_at/expires_at), the certification state (ADR-066) and a record_hash over the whole. It asserts exactly 'this implementation passed this profile version with this evidence, in this scope, until this date'.
concepts.normative_source: ADR-064 D-064-03, ADR-066, contracts/production/certification-record.production.schema.json
relations: governed by the closed certification-state machine (ADR-066)

concepts.name: certification lifecycle
concepts.short_def: The closed, Rust-decided state machine governing a certificate's standing over time.
concepts.full_def: The certification lifecycle is a closed, total, deterministic state machine with a fixed transition table decided only by the Rust engine. States: NOT_CERTIFIED (fail-closed default), CERTIFIED, EXPIRED, SUSPENDED, REVOKED, SUPERSEDED. Only CERTIFIED (within scope+window, evidence reproduces) reads as valid; everything else is not-certified. REVOKED is terminal; renewal is a brand-new record (never an in-place extension). No human/model/config may effect, widen or reverse a transition, and no L2 transition propagates to L3 admission or regulator.
relations: transitions computed by engines/banza-conformance / certification engine

concepts.name: trust
concepts.short_def: Open Trust Evaluation: deterministic, local, human-free verification of whether to route to a peer.
concepts.full_def: Trust in BANZA is the Open Trust Evaluation = Public Registry metadata + Signed Protocol Metadata + conformance evidence, verified against root-endorsed delegated keys with fail-closed semantics and no BANZA-issued artifact about an operator and no human step. It replaces the retired central-authority certificate-dependent trust protocol; a peer computes the answer locally, offline, with no central lookup.
concepts.normative_source: ADR-038 (Open Trust Model without CA, INV-OTE-001..008), ADR-040 (federation trust evaluation), ADR-058 (INV-OTE registry realignment)
relations: consumes Signed Protocol Metadata + key manifest + revocation

concepts.name: revocation
concepts.short_def: Signed, dated withdrawal of keys/artifacts (or a certificate) — a security/trust mechanism, not a licence or sanction.
concepts.full_def: Revocation is the signed, dated withdrawal of protocol keys/artifacts via the public Revocation List (a Trust-Root-signed object), and of certificates via the certification-state machine (CERTIFIED|SUSPENDED|EXPIRED -> REVOKED, terminal). It is a protocol security and trust mechanism, never a licence, regulatory sanction or financial authorisation. Fail-closed: a peer that cannot obtain and verify a fresh signed list treats material as untrusted, never as an empty list.
concepts.normative_source: ADR-038 (Revocation List), ADR-040, ADR-066 D-066-03, contracts/production/revocation-entry.production.schema.json, contracts/federation/revocation-list.json
relations: input to the Open Trust Evaluation
REVOKED certificate never resurrects (new record only)

concepts.name: Evidence Bundle
concepts.short_def: A reproducible package of hashed artifacts/status references — a package of inputs, not a certificate.
concepts.full_def: An Evidence Bundle binds the hashed artifacts and status references (readiness, assurance, M2 protocol-gate, conformance report) that a candidate publishes as verifiable conformance evidence. It is reproducible and independently checkable, and by itself grants nothing: it is NOT a certificate. It must verify against the public key material bound in the manifest it names, and its manifest_hash must bind to that manifest.
concepts.normative_source: ADR-038 INV-OTE-002, contracts/production/evidence-bundle.production.schema.json

concepts.name: Technical Registry
concepts.short_def: The single public, root-verifiable index of L2 artifacts — strictly independent of any scheme's participant directory.
concepts.full_def: The BANZA Technical Registry is the single public, append-mostly, root-verifiable index of L2 artifacts — implementations, certification profiles, certification records and their revocations — verifiable by any third party with no account and no trust in any operator's word. It answers 'is this implementation certified, against what profile, in what scope, until when, still valid?'. It is strictly independent of the L3 scheme participant directory: 'listed in the technical registry' is never 'admitted to a scheme' or 'authorised'. Today it is empty (/operators returns []).
concepts.normative_source: ADR-065 (D-065-*), ADR-059 D-059-07, contracts/production/public-protocol-registry.production.schema.json
concepts.canonical_page: /operadores (registry surface) — a dedicated /registo page is MISSING
relations: distinct from L3 Banzami Scheme Participant Directory (ADR-060 D-060-06)

concepts.name: federation
concepts.short_def: Interoperation between operators by published evidence + Open Trust Evaluation — not per-pair bilateral contracts.
concepts.full_def: Federation is the routing of payments between independent operators established by published, verifiable evidence and the Open Trust Evaluation over signed metadata, rather than a bilateral contract per operator pair. It requires the applicable conformance scope, valid+fresh signed metadata/evidence, absence from the Revocation List and the production conditions. Production federation is not active in pre-production.
concepts.normative_source: ADR-040 (federation trust evaluation without certificates), contracts/federation/*.json, ch.10
relations: depends on conformance scope + trust + revocation

concepts.name: BanzAI
concepts.short_def: The single human-operator interface at /banzai — transversal across the three layers, NOT a layer or authority.
concepts.full_def: BanzAI is the canonical human interface through which people run every human workflow across the three layers (ask + the 9-step validation journey). It orients and executes by calling the Rust engines and explains once with local Qwen; it never decides, certifies, admits, publishes, activates funds or changes a state/reason code. One app, two modes, one route (/banzai). Machine/SDK consumers keep direct API access — BanzAI is the human plane, not a mandatory gate and NOT a fourth layer/authority.
concepts.normative_source: ADR-054 (primary human-operator interface), ADR-050 (unified same-origin interface), ADR-049 (agent core), ADR-067 D-067-02/03, ADR-059 D-059-04
forbidden_terms: camada oficial de orientação e orquestração
relations: qwen_calls:0 / external_calls:0 in validation mode by construction

concepts.name: Operador Zero
concepts.short_def: The single canonical read-only reference implementation, validated only in BanzAI validation mode.
concepts.full_def: Operador Zero is the read-only canonical reference implementation on zero.banza.network. It exposes identity, manifest, capabilities, endpoints, metadata, public keys, reports, evidence and certification status and nothing else — no simulation, no mutable ledger, no self-execution, no self-certification. It is validated exclusively via /banzai?mode=validation&target=operator-zero&workflow=full. Demo-only, no real funds, NOT_CERTIFIED / PRE_PRODUCTION, never in /operators, never a scheme participant.
concepts.normative_source: ADR-067 (read-only reference + BanzAI validation), ADR-052, ADR-053
relations: only validation target (closed registry in banzaiValidation.ts)
the reference chapter ch.9 must be rewritten from ADR-052 simulator framing to ADR-067 read-only reference

concepts.name: Banzami Operational Scheme
concepts.short_def: Layer 3: the first operational scheme on BANZA, with Banzami as the designated operator, in regulatory preparation.
concepts.full_def: The Banzami Operational Scheme is the first operational scheme built on BANZA (Layer 3), promoted, designed and administered by Banzami — Tecnologia e Serviços, Lda. as the designated operator, conditioned on obtaining the applicable regulatory framework. Its state is REGULATORY_AUTHORIZATION_IN_PROGRESS; real funds, wallets, settlement and real participants are fail-closed until formal evidence exists. BANZA != Banzami and BANZA certification is not exclusive to this scheme.
concepts.normative_source: ADR-060 (designated operator; BANZA != Banzami), ADR-059 D-059-03, ADR-062 (regulatory-state), ADR-063 (conflict of interest/separation)
relations: owns the L3 participant directory (distinct from L2 registry)
does not appear as a public surface in ~/banza except as a described layer

concepts.name: scheme admission
concepts.short_def: A scheme's own determination that an entity/implementation is admitted as its participant — separate from certification.
concepts.full_def: Scheme Admission is a determination by the Banzami Operational Scheme (or any independent scheme) that a specific entity/implementation is admitted as a participant of that scheme, on the scheme's own due diligence, eligibility and contracts. It is a separate, later step that MAY require valid certification as a prerequisite but is never implied by it. Certification alone admits no one; admission is not regulatory authorisation.

concepts.name: regulatory authorisation
concepts.short_def: The competent regulator's grant to conduct regulated financial activity — BANZA is not a party to it.
concepts.full_def: Regulatory Authorisation is granted by the competent regulator to an operator/participant under the applicable legal framework to conduct regulated financial activity. BANZA is not a party: it does not grant, hold, represent, accelerate or substitute for it, issues no licences and replaces no regulator. Certification (L2) and scheme admission (L3) never imply it.
concepts.normative_source: ADR-061 D-061-03/05, ADR-062 (regulatory-state boundary + RealMoneyActivationGate), ADR-059 D-059-01
relations: decided by the competent regulator only
gated by the RealMoneyActivationGate (ADR-062) which keeps real money OFF

concepts.name: pre-production
concepts.short_def: The honest current state: spec frozen, registry empty, no production keys/certificates, no real money.
concepts.full_def: Pre-production is the protocol's current maturity state: spec v1.0 frozen; /operators returns []; production_certificates=false; trust metadata pending the offline root-key ceremony (M2); no production federation; and the L3 scheme at REGULATORY_AUTHORIZATION_IN_PROGRESS with every real-money capability fail-closed. Machine routes return honest envelopes; an empty registry is the correct state, not a failure.
concepts.normative_source: ADR-031 (canonical verification routes and pre-production), ADR-062 (regulatory-state baseline), contracts/production/regulatory-state.production.schema.json
relations: mirrored by the machine routes (verifiable source)

concepts.name: OperationReceipt
concepts.short_def: A per-step, verifiable record of one validation-journey step: what ran, what the Rust engine decided, with metadata.
concepts.full_def: An OperationReceipt is the per-step artifact emitted for each of the nine validation steps: it records the step, the Rust-decided outcome/reason, the execution-path metadata (qwen_calls, external_calls) and the inputs/hashes, so each step is independently readable. Qwen explains it; Rust decides it.
concepts.normative_source: ADR-067 (9-step journey, OperationReceipt per step), ADR-051 (per-answer execution-path metadata), website/lib/operationReceipt.ts, website/components/banzai/validationJourney.tsx

concepts.name: JourneyReceipt
concepts.short_def: The aggregate, verifiable record of a full 9-step validation journey and its overall readiness outcome.
concepts.full_def: A JourneyReceipt aggregates the nine OperationReceipts of a validation journey into one verifiable record of the whole run — the ordered steps, their Rust-decided outcomes and the overall certification-readiness result — without itself being a certificate or a grant. It is the session-level evidence of what was validated, for whom (target=operator-zero), and how.
concepts.normative_source: ADR-067 (JourneyReceipt), website/lib/operationReceipt.ts, website/components/banzai/BanzaiValidationMode.tsx
relations: distinct from a CertificationRecord (evidence of a run, not a verdict object)

concepts.name: reason code
concepts.short_def: A closed-enum machine-readable code explaining a Rust-decided verdict or state transition.
concepts.full_def: A reason code is a machine-readable value from a closed enum that explains a Rust-decided outcome. For certification the CertificationRecord reason_code enum is OK_CONFORMANT_INTEROPERABLE plus FAIL_SCHEMA_INVALID, FAIL_CANONICALIZATION_INVALID, FAIL_HASH_MISMATCH, FAIL_SIGNATURE_INVALID, FAIL_IDENTITY_INVALID, FAIL_PROFILE_MISMATCH, FAIL_PROTOCOL_MISMATCH, FAIL_ENVIRONMENT_MISMATCH, FAIL_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED, FAIL_CONFORMANCE, FAIL_INTEROPERABILITY, FAIL_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE, FAIL_EVIDENCE_EXPIRED, FAIL_TRUST_INVALID, FAIL_REVOKED, FAIL_VALIDITY_WINDOW, FAIL_ILLEGAL_TRANSITION. Reason codes are part of L1's public vocabulary; the local model never invents or changes one.
concepts.normative_source: ADR-064/ADR-066, contracts/production/certification-record.production.schema.json (reason_code enum), ADR-059 D-059-01 (reason codes are L1 vocabulary)

notes.L0_L4_clarification: L0-L4 remain valid as CONFORMANCE SCOPE LEVELS inside the L2 certification model (ADR-021; certification-profile.conformance_level; certification-record.scope_levels enum L0-L4). What M2.19G forbids is presenting L0-L4 as public CERTIFICATION LEVELS/TIERS (the retired framing in reference ch.7 'Níveis L0-L4'). 'Layer 2 (L2)' in ADR-064's title is the SECOND institutional LAYER, not a level.
notes.missing_owner_pages: certification/CertifiedImplementation/CertificationRecord/CertificationProfile/certification lifecycle/reason code currently have NO real owning page: /certificacao and /conformidade both redirect to the reference chapter /referencia/certificacao, whose content still describes the retired L0-L4 model. The Technical Registry has no dedicated /registo page (only /operadores). A public glossary owning these definitions does not exist.
